content: {"rule": "K-C", "applies": "yes", "applies_why": "The judge text addresses a collision over the Isaiah 7:14 link where the challenger presses the sign's own bounds and the defender answers with a read-together chain, so K-C governs how that collision is weighed.", "verdict": "BREACH", "quote": "the sign itself does not state the mechanism.", "rule_words": "When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.", "room": "The phrase 'never verse by verse' had to be read against the judge's phrase 'the sign itself does not state the mechanism': one reading treats the judge as making an impermissible single-verse test of the link; the other treats it as merely describing the sign while otherwise weighing the chains by footing.", "why": "The judge resolves the link by noting what Isaiah 7:14 itself does not state rather than weighing the competing chains by footing, which is the verse-by-verse/stating-verse approach K-C retires."}
